questions.q: Why do sparse rewards make learning slow?
options: Because the discount factor must be set to zero
Because a near-random early policy rarely stumbles onto the rare nonzero reward, leaving no gradient signal until it does
Because sparse rewards are always negative
Because sparse rewards require continuous action spaces
questions.explain: When reward is zero almost everywhere, early training provides no useful signal to distinguish better trajectories from worse ones until the agent happens to reach the rare rewarding event.

questions.q: What is the general reward shaping formula?
options: r'(s,a,s') = r(s,a,s') + F(s,s'), where F is an auxiliary shaping term
r'(s,a,s') = max(r(s,a,s'), 0)
r'(s,a,s') = γ · r(s,a,s')
questions.explain: Reward shaping adds an auxiliary term F(s, s') to the environment's true reward to densify the signal.

questions.q: What does potential-based shaping, F(s,s') = γΦ(s') − Φ(s), guarantee?
options: It guarantees the agent reaches the goal in the fewest possible steps
It guarantees faster convergence but makes no promise about the optimal policy
It guarantees that the optimal policy under the shaped reward is the same as the optimal policy under the original reward
It guarantees the reward is always positive
questions.explain: Ng, Harada, and Russell's 1999 shaping theorem shows potential-based shaping can only change how fast an optimal policy is found, never which policy is optimal.

questions.q: Why is an arbitrary, non-potential-based shaping term riskier?
options: It is always slower than no shaping at all
It carries no guarantee against changing the optimal policy, so the agent can learn to exploit the shaping term instead of the real task
It cannot be implemented in Python
It only works with Discrete action spaces
questions.explain: Without the potential-based structure, a shaping term can become the de facto objective, causing the agent to optimize it instead of the designer's actual intent.

questions.q: In the distance-based shaping example, what role does gamma play in shaped_reward()?
options: It is the learning rate for the neural network
It is the same discount factor used elsewhere in the MDP, applied to the potential of the next state before subtracting the potential of the current state
It has no role and can be removed safely
It converts the reward into a probability
questions.explain: Potential-based shaping is defined as F(s,s') = γΦ(s') − Φ(s), using the MDP's own discount factor to keep the guarantee intact.
